passage.text: There is an important pattern in serious port accidents. Reports tend to show that the most dangerous incidents often happen where two groups of workers meet without clear communication. For example, ship workers and the workers who load and unload cargo may share the same space. Each group usually has a good system on its own. However, the problem tends to appear at the point where their systems connect. This interface, where responsibility moves from one party to another, seems to be where things go wrong most often.

source.title: Port and Harbour Safety: Risks and Controls Explained
